subject: general
question: What is the name given to a saucer-shaped intrusive igneous body that is concave to the sky?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lopolith**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **lopolith** is a saucer-shaped intrusive igneous rock body that has a concave shape facing upwards (towards the sky).
 
• It forms when magma intrudes between layers of sedimentary rock and cools, causing the layers above it to sag.
 
• Lopoliths are typically composed of mafic or ultramafic rocks, such as gabbro or anorthosite.
 
• They are associated with large igneous provinces and are considered important for understanding geological processes of magma emplacement.
 
• Examples of lopoliths include the Bushveld Complex in South Africa, which is one of the largest known lopoliths and a significant source of platinum group elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sill:**

 
 
• A sill is a flat, horizontal, or nearly horizontal sheet of igneous rock that forms when magma intrudes parallel to the bedding planes of sedimentary rocks.
 
• Sills are concordant intrusions, meaning they do not cut through the layers of rock they intrude.
 
• They differ from lopoliths in their flat shape and lack of sagging caused in the overlying rock layers.
 
 
 
• **Phacolith:**
 
 
• A phacolith is an igneous intrusion that forms in the crests of anticlines or troughs of synclines (geological folds).
 
• It typically has a lens-like or crescent-shaped appearance.
 
• Phacoliths are usually smaller in size compared to lopoliths and are associated with folded sedimentary rocks.
 
 
 
• **Batholith:**
 
 
• A batholith is a large, irregularly shaped mass of intrusive igneous rock that has solidified deep beneath the Earth's surface.
 
• Batholiths are massive and can cover hundreds of square kilometers, often forming the cores of mountain ranges.
 
• An example is the Sierra Nevada Batholith in the western United States.
